Plot directions of movement in an ordination

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/plotDirection.R
plotDirection.Rd

plotDirection() draws a rose diagram of the directions in which subjects move between consecutive samples in two components of a reduced dimension.

plotDirection(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
plotDirection(
  x,
  time.col,
  group,
  dimred,
  ncomponents = c(1, 2),
  bins = 16,
  group.by = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a SingleCellExperiment object, such as a TreeSummarizedExperiment.

...

additional arguments passed to geom_histogram.

time.col

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that contains sampling times: numeric, Date or a factor of visits.

group

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that identifies subjects.

dimred

Character scalar. Specifies the reducedDim(x) to use.

ncomponents

Numeric or Character vector. The two components of dimred, by index or name. (Default: c(1, 2))

bins

Integer scalar. Number of direction sectors. (Default: 16)

group.by

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that splits the moves into panels. Each move takes the value of its earlier sample. (Default: NULL)

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Angles are measured counterclockwise from the first component (east), so 90 degrees points along the second component. Moves of zero length have no direction and are left out.

Examples

# Directions in a PCoA of three bioreactors
data("minimalgut", package = "miaTime")
tse <- mia::transformAssay(minimalgut, method = "relabundance")
tse <- mia::addMDS(tse, assay.type = "relabundance", method = "bray",
    name = "PCoA")
plotDirection(tse, time.col = "Time.hr", group = "StudyIdentifier",
    dimred = "PCoA", group.by = "StudyIdentifier")
